title: Man arrested in bed after West Seattle break-in, police say
dek: Police say a 41-year-old man tried to enter one home and broke into another near Fauntleroy Way SW on Sunday afternoon.
body: Seattle police arrested a 41-year-old man Sunday afternoon after he broke into a West Seattle home and was found lying in a bed inside, FOX 13 reported, citing police and the King County Prosecuting Attorney's Office.

Officers were called at about 2 p.m. to a reported burglary in progress at a home on Fauntleroy Way SW near SW Webster St. According to police, the man went into a woman's backyard and asked her for a blanket. When she said she did not have one, he became agitated and tried to get in through the basement and back door. The homeowner called 911 while he was pulling at the door.

Police said the man then went to a different home near SW Austin St and kicked in the back door, breaking the lock. No one was home. Inside, according to FOX 13, he drank milk and ate bananas in the kitchen before getting into a bed.
Officers surrounded the house and called out to him but got no answer. They went inside, found him under the covers and arrested him.

He was booked into the King County Jail for investigation of residential burglary and attempted residential burglary, with bail set at $25,000. Probable cause documents say he also had an active warrant out of Kent for fourth-degree assault and failure to appear, FOX 13 reported. He had not been formally charged as of the report, and his name was not released.

title: Man charged in 2024 South Park kidnapping and rape
dek: Prosecutors say a conviction could expose the 58-year-old, who has prior sex-offense convictions, to life without parole.
body: A 58-year-old man has been charged in King County Superior Court with first-degree kidnapping with sexual motivation and second-degree rape in connection with an alleged November 2024 attack in South Park, Hoodline reported, citing KING 5.

Orhan H. Najaar was arrested Oct. 8 and charged Oct. 13. According to the woman's account to investigators, he forced her into a vehicle at knifepoint on Nov. 19, 2024, as she returned from a doctor's appointment, then took her to her apartment, where she says he raped her repeatedly and punched her. Hospital records from the next day noted swelling near her eye and jaw and wrist pain.

She reported the alleged assault to police in May 2026. Investigators sent a tool bag collected from her apartment to the Washington State Crime Lab; results were pending when charges were filed. According to KING 5, Najaar acknowledged sex with the woman but described it as consensual and denied kidnapping her.
Court records reviewed by KING 5 show prior guilty pleas in 2008, 2012 and 2019 cases involving third-degree rape and sexually motivated assault. He was released from prison Oct. 7, 2024.
Prosecutors asked that bail remain at $2 million and argued a conviction could count as a third strike, carrying life without parole. The charges are allegations and the case is pending.

title: Belltown business owners describe open-air drug market on 2nd Ave
dek: Owners near 2nd Ave between Bell and Blanchard report a daytime drug market and sidewalk encampment as Mayor Katie Wilson faces public safety questions.
body: Business owners near 2nd Ave between Bell and Blanchard streets in Belltown say a daytime open-air drug market and a sidewalk encampment have formed in the area, KOMO reported. Several described a recent trend but declined to speak on the record.
The block once housed the Crocodile Cafe and Mama's Mexican Kitchen.

The reports come as Mayor Katie Wilson faces questions after a weekend of shootings across the city, including two homicides. "Obviously, public safety is on a lot of people's minds with good reason," Wilson said, according to KOMO. She said the city is developing neighborhood-based public safety plans and named Belltown as an area with persistent concerns.

Wilson said her proposed budget funds 66 more police officers next year. A Seattle Metro Chamber survey of 700 voters cited by KOMO found 86% said shutting down open-air drug markets should be a priority.

title: Man accused in CID Metro bus machete attack leaves home detention

body: A 30-year-old man charged in a July 2 machete attack on a King County Metro Route 7 bus in the Chinatown-International District has left electronic home detention without approval, and his whereabouts are unknown, KOMO reported.

Prosecutors allege Daniel Couch damaged the bus with a machete after the driver refused to let him board because he was armed, shattering two side windows and cracking the windshield. The bus was taken out of service. No injuries were reported.

Couch is charged with second-degree malicious mischief and pleaded not guilty July 9. An Aug. 21 court document found him in violation of home detention conditions, but on Sept. 15 a judge granted temporary release to electronic home detention so he could receive treatment.

According to the Department of Adult and Juvenile Detention, a monitoring device showed he left his required location on Sunday, and he did not respond to a caseworker. A court entry dated Oct. 12 says he left without an approved pass. The court will determine next steps, which could include an arrest warrant.

title: White-powder letter forces partial evacuation of downtown federal building
dek: A letter containing white powder was found on the floor of the Henry M. Jackson Federal Building that houses Sen. Maria Cantwell's offices, part of what the FBI describes as a nationwide investigation.
body: A suspicious letter containing white powder was found on the afternoon of Oct. 15 on the 32nd floor of the Henry M. Jackson Federal Building in downtown Seattle, KOMO News reported. The floor, which houses Sen. Maria Cantwell's offices, was partially evacuated as a precaution.
Fire officials said the substance was contained and removed, and the area was declared safe to reoccupy. No injuries were reported.

The same afternoon, a second white-powder letter addressed to the Washington Secretary of State's elections division in Olympia was intercepted by state Department of Enterprise Services staff before it reached the office. On Oct. 16, U.S. Rep. Pramila Jayapal's Seattle office received a suspicious package. Jayapal said she and her staff were safe.
Secretary of State Steve Hobbs condemned the Olympia letter as a terrorist attack meant to create confusion, chaos and fear among election workers, according to KOMO.

The FBI says the incidents are part of a nationwide investigation into suspicious mail sent to election offices and congressional addresses. Federal authorities have not said what the powder in the Washington cases was and are working to identify the sender or senders.
KOMO reported similar incidents this week in Louisiana, Oklahoma, Ohio and Wisconsin, where testing found the powder in one letter was not hazardous. The mailings come weeks before Election Day.

title: Man charged with assault in Hing Hay Park machete attack
dek: King County prosecutors charged a 44-year-old man with first- and second-degree assault after two men were slashed in the Chinatown-International District park.
body: King County prosecutors have charged Oneil George Bygrave, 44, with first- and second-degree assault in a machete attack on two men at Hing Hay Park in the Chinatown-International District, FOX 13 reported.

Police responded to an assault in progress around 5 p.m. Oct. 6. According to investigators, two men Bygrave did not know told him to leave the park, and the verbal argument ended with him pulling a machete and slashing both. One man suffered a large cut to the head; the other had large cuts to his upper back and wrist.

Seattle police Real Time Crime Center cameras partially captured the attack, according to charging information cited by FOX 13. The video shows the suspect chasing one victim and continuing to swing at a victim on the ground before another person spoke to him and the attack ended.
Officers found Bygrave still in the park holding the machete. He briefly hid behind bushes and then came out without it, and officers recovered the weapon.
At an Oct. 14 hearing, a judge denied his request for release, calling him an extreme danger, and kept bail at $500,000. He remains in the King County Jail.

title: 25 years on, investigators say Tom Wales killing is 'not a cold case'
dek: Crime Stoppers says the FBI and Seattle police are still actively working the 2001 shooting of the federal prosecutor in his Queen Anne home, with up to $2.5 million offered for information.
body: Nearly 25 years after federal prosecutor Tom Wales was shot inside his Queen Anne home, investigators say the case remains active, according to Crime Stoppers of Puget Sound, as reported by MyNorthwest.
Wales, a senior federal prosecutor in Seattle for nearly two decades, was shot in his basement office at about 10:40 p.m. and died the next day. No one has been arrested.

"They wanted to stress the point that they are actively working this, that this is not a cold case at this point," Crime Stoppers Executive Director Jim Fuda told the outlet. The FBI, Seattle Police Department, U.S. Department of Justice and King County Prosecutor's Office are involved in the investigation.

According to the report, investigators have examined whether someone followed Wales home or otherwise learned where he lived. A letter received in 2006 indicated the writer knew Wales' wife was not home at the time of the shooting. "I'm guessing there must have been some surveillance on him that followed him home," Fuda said.

Wales had prosecuted a helicopter company accused of violating federal aviation standards; the company pleaded guilty to misdemeanor FAA violations in 2001. Fuda described Wales as "a white-collar crime prosecutor and an avid advocate for gun control."
A reward of up to $2.5 million is offered for information leading to an arrest. Tips can go to the FBI, to Crime Stoppers of Puget Sound at 1-800-222-TIPS, or through the P3 Tips app.

body: Two people who appeared to be trying to steal fuel from parked rental trucks set off an early-morning fire that burned three box trucks in SoDo on Friday, Sept. 25, Seattle police said, according to KOMO.

Firefighters responded around 1:30 a.m. to the Penske rental truck facility at 1st Avenue South and South Spokane Street and found three box trucks on fire. Crews knocked the fire down in about half an hour and protected nearby buildings. No injuries were reported. Police estimated more than $150,000 in damage to the empty trucks.

Officers initially detained and arrested a 37-year-old man found near the lot's fence line after a witness said he had seen him near where the fire started. Later that morning, Arson Bomb Squad detectives reviewed the business's security footage, determined he was not involved and released him from King County Jail.

According to police, the footage showed a vehicle arrive with two suspects who appeared to be trying to steal fuel when the fire ignited. The flames engulfed the suspects and their vehicle, which then drove out of the fire and left southbound on 1st Avenue South. Detectives believe one suspect may have a heat injury or singed hair and eyebrows.
The suspects have not been located. Police released an image of the suspect vehicle and ask anyone with information to call the Seattle Police tip line at (206) 233-5000.

body: Two men were wounded when gunfire broke out at a late-night street party at Kerry Park on Queen Anne early Saturday, Oct. 10, KOMO News reported. Police were called around 3:30 a.m. after multiple people reported shots fired.

A homeowner's security camera captured a burst of gunfire around 3:29 a.m., followed by two cars speeding away. Officers found 50 shell casings of both rifle and handgun calibers, and at least one vehicle was damaged.

The two men had left the scene and arrived separately at Harborview Medical Center, one shot in the leg and the other in the hip. Police first described both as in serious but stable condition; by noon Saturday a hospital spokesperson said both were in satisfactory condition.

Officers stopped a vehicle and detained everyone inside after seeing a rifle and other evidence. One juvenile was arrested for assault and booked into the Judge Patricia H. Clark Children and Family Justice Center. Police seized the vehicle and planned to seek a search warrant. Gun Violence Reduction Unit detectives are investigating.

Nearby residents told KOMO that large gatherings in the street and park have become more frequent since summer 2025. "We want to intervene, before there's 50 shell casings left on the ground," resident Brad Heisinger said.

body: King County prosecutors have charged Kamilia Chadli, 36, with second-degree assault in connection with a Sept. 18 attack outside the Arctic Hotel on Cherry Street downtown, KOMO News reported. She was initially held on suspicion of a hate crime.

Chadli was detained minutes later at a bus stop outside the King County Courthouse. Witnesses' accounts contradict her version, KOMO reported. She denied making comments about race.

A judge ordered a mental competency evaluation at the defense's request. Her next court appearance was set for Oct. 13. Court records describe a lengthy history of police contacts and a prior emergency mental health detention, according to KOMO.

title: Family seeks $30 million over fatal police shooting behind Southwest Precinct
dek: Relatives of Andrew Seay, shot by a Seattle officer in March 2025, filed a claim alleging negligence, excessive force and disability-law violations.
body: The family of Andrew Seay, 36, who was shot and killed by a Seattle police officer in March 2025 in a restricted parking lot behind the Southwest Precinct, has filed a $30 million claim against the city, Hoodline reported.

According to the report, Seay's wife called 911 at 12:16 p.m. on March 19, 2025, saying he was in mental distress and making suicidal statements. Seay had a folding pocketknife, and body-camera video shows officers repeatedly ordering him to drop it. A 40 mm less-lethal launcher was fired but did not stop him, and one officer fired his handgun just before 12:30 p.m. Seay died at the scene.

The claim, filed by attorneys Mark Lindquist and Angus Lee, alleges negligence, excessive force and violation of the Americans with Disabilities Act. It disputes that Seay posed an immediate threat, and argues officers could have kept their distance, continued de-escalating and used vehicles for cover. Accounts of the distance between Seay and the officer when shots were fired range from more than 30 feet to 35 feet.

The King County Prosecuting Attorney's Office declined to file criminal charges. The family's attorneys say that decision does not settle civil liability, and that a lawsuit can be filed 60 days after the claim. Hoodline did not report a city response to the claim.

body: Seattle police are asking for help identifying a driver who a 25-year-old woman says posed as her Uber driver after she left a Pioneer Square bar, KOMO News reported on Oct. 19.

The woman told police she had been at a bar in the 400 block of 1st Avenue South on Oct. 10 and ordered an Uber. When a car pulled up, she asked the driver whether it was for her and he said yes. She did not check the plate or the driver's name before getting in.

According to the report, the driver passed her exit, and she then received a notice that her Uber ride had been canceled. She saw that he was navigating with Google Maps rather than the Uber app and texted friends. She believed he left the freeway at Exit 156 in Kent. When the car stopped at a red light, she jumped out and ran, and the driver sped off. Friends found her near Military Road South and Kent Des Moines Road.
She described the car as a white four-door sedan and the driver as a Black man between 30 and 50 years old. She did not get the plate number.

Police asked the Real Time Crime Center for video, but SPD cameras in the area were not working and recorded nothing, KOMO reported. No arrest has been reported. Police asked anyone with information to call the Violent Crimes Tip Line at (206) 233-5000.

item_headline: City Attorney adds prosecutors for Aurora trafficking, gun cases
title: City Attorney adds prosecutors for Aurora trafficking and gun cases
dek: Seattle City Attorney Erika Evans announced two dedicated prosecutor positions aimed at sex trafficking on Aurora Avenue North and at firearms.
body: Seattle City Attorney Erika Evans announced two new dedicated prosecutor positions on Oct. 14 aimed at crime along Aurora Avenue North, FOX 13 reported.

One prosecutor will be cross-deputized with the King County Prosecuting Attorney's Office to handle both misdemeanor and felony cases against pimps, buyers and human traffickers on the corridor. Historically the county has handled felony prosecutions while the City Attorney's Office was limited to misdemeanors; Evans said the new positions let the city take on felony-level work.

The second prosecutor will lead a new Firearms Unit that will seek civil Extreme Risk Protection Orders to remove guns from people considered a significant threat, working with the Regional Domestic Violence Firearms Enforcement Unit.

Both positions are funded in Mayor Katie Wilson's proposed budget, according to FOX 13. King County Prosecuting Attorney Leesa Manion and SPD Interim Chief Andre Sayles expressed support. Officials noted that trafficking cases are difficult to build: over the past five years, an average of six cases a year in Seattle met the evidence threshold for charges.
Some residents remain skeptical. A start date for the positions was not reported.
